[[File:John Arendt DecipherCon 1999 SAT.jpg|thumb|right|260px|John Arendt at DecipherCon 1999. Photo: Decipher.]]
'''John Arendt''' finished first in the Wild Card of the [[1999 Decipher World Championship]].<ref name="rfd112" /> He was the first [[Players Committee]] [[Tournament Advocate]] (Tournament Support), named by Warren Holland on 25 January 2002.<ref name="pc1" /> He was also a Decipher-era [[Squadron Members|Squadron Member]], listed as Bravo 16 from Boulder, Co. The published fan table marks the slot Retired after Decipher's SWCCG run.

Decipher recruited volunteer Squadron Members in the 1990s to promote SWCCG locally (tournaments, demos, player support). "FL" is printed on some slots in the surviving tables.

== Radio Free Decipher (2002) ==

On ''[[Radio Free Decipher]]'' Broadcast 112 (25 January 2002), [[Scott Gaeta]] called Arendt one of the most underrated players in the world. Gaeta said Colorado players had coined the term "Arendt tech" for his unusual, original deck ideas. Host [[Kyle Heuer]] said Arendt would handle tournament programs for the [[Players Committee]].<ref name="rfd112">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=docK2vpQWUI&t=880s Broadcast 112 - Radio Free Decipher (25 January, 2002): Scott Gaeta on the SWCCG PC], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 13 May 2022), at 14:40. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-docK2vpQWUI Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 112 transcript]].</ref>
